title: aider-builds-a-piece
intention: Give the aider shim a builder loop: carry ONE piece of a cast ticket from its berthed brief to an applied edit plus a run test result. It runs inside the shim's own venv interpreter (the only place aider is importable with our surfaces standing), calls translate.brief() for the prompt and file lists, calls holder.hold(), constructs aider's Coder from the brief's fields (map_tokens=0, auto_commits OFF), runs one edit pass confined to brief.files, runs the piece's test_cmd, and returns serializable data. It STAMPS THE TICKET on every recorded ask — a field fence.SeenLog.record already takes and nothing supplies. It does NOT write a verdict artifact and crosses nothing: disposing the result stays CC's act at /sail step 6.
why: The shim is complete and INERT — zero callers repo-wide outside its own folder, and translate.py says the gap in its own words: 'A brief is data; running it is someone else's.' There is no someone else, so offloading a build to the apprentice cannot happen, and therefore cannot be measured. Law 1 is the aim (the resolver spent on the novel; a mechanical piece built from a settled chart chain is the definition of not-novel) and Law 3 is the urgency (hypothesis 8 — does offloading yield? — was marked CARRIED at aider-shim's verdict and stays unmeasured until a real ticket goes through). The measured symptom: the offload probe reads shimmed:0, rows:0, and its population is empty BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by nothing-having-happened-yet — all four allowed asks in the log carry ticket:'', because the live fire drove a synthetic piece and nothing else has ever driven anything.
traces_to: Telos 1 (demonstrate inference compilation) and Telos 5 (self-improving — the system building itself with a cheaper hand). Law 1 as the operative one. Law 3 for the measurement it unblocks. Law 8 for the shape of the watch: a green earned by the supervisor rather than the apprentice is a hollow green, and hollow green is worse here than red.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam@v2 invariant: proved + feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). ENTRY at BUILDME: refuses without a berthed validate packet claiming this ticket (buildme-rides-the-chart) and without intent_berth + sorted_berth — which for this node is not ceremony, since survey is where the venv/test-runnability assumption gets measured. PROVE at PROVEME: tester runs the proofs beside the code, netns isolation, sink='validations'. EXIT at PROVED: refuses without a complete passing verdict artifact answering every criterion of the claiming validate berth by its instrument (proved-answers-the-chart). EMISSION at WATCHME: refuses unless a module declaring a frozen module-level PROBE stands at the probe berth above. KICKS BACK ON: a red proof (back-edge to BUILDME); a failed criterion at step 6 is a kick-back, not a crossing. Check-type is machine throughout — proved by running the code, never by review.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a real cast ticket's piece is carried brief -> applied edit -> run test result, with the ask recorded carrying that ticket, and the offload probe's `shimmed` count moves off 0 (measured at 0 today). WRONG-INTENT when the driven edits need rewriting by CC more often than they survive, or when supervising a driven piece costs more tool calls than building it by hand would have — either kills the offload thesis, and the driver is then the instrument that killed it rather than a failed build.
falsifier.horizon: Re-read when the first real ticket has been driven, OR on 2026-09-16 (30 days) if nothing has been driven by then. The second clause is the real one: a driver nobody drives is the same failure mode as an armed probe nobody fires, and this device already owns one of those.

The build, one commit '6d3e689b0bf8: build — the probe returns to its berth': git mv cairn/devices/aider_shim/probes_disabled/edit_survival_probe.py cairn/devices/aider_shim/probes/edit_survival_probe.py (mkdir probes first) and git mv cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs_disabled/test_edit_survival_probe.py cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_edit_survival_probe.py; then in proofs/test_edit_survival_probe.py, inside test_the_probe_is_armed_at_the_path_the_TICKET_names, replace the stale ticket path Path.home()/'dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/aider-builds-a-piece.json' with Path(ticket_path('6d3e689b0bf8')), adding 'from cairn.tools.chain.grammar import ticket_path' inside that tooth (tickets are now named <id>-<slug>.json). Measured 2026-10-13: with the files restored, that tooth is the proof's only red. Nothing else changes. Proof: cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_edit_survival_probe.py. Then PROVEME --proven-by it, hollow seal, verdict, WATCHME (the probe is armed at the ticket's berth), PROVED. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09; approved thru PROVED (Akien 2026-10-12)

This build adds the probe at probes/, so PROVEME's proof_binds_its_subject_at_call_time (cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py:647) reds that line and the hollow would read UNRAN. In the moved proof, that line becomes exactly 'probe = None  # bound in main(): this build adds the probe, so the hollow takes it away', and the first two lines of the body of the main function at line 280 become 'global probe' and a try: 'from cairn.devices.aider_shim.probes import edit_survival_probe as probe' / except ImportError: pass — so with the probe reverted each tooth fails on its own (None has no attribute) and prints red. No other line of the proof changes beyond D1's ticket path.
